issue: When a post-plea government intrusion into attorney-client communications violates the Sixth Amendment, who bears the burden of proving prejudice or the lack of prejudice?

sides.position: The defendant must show actual prejudice from the intrusion.
cases: Cutillo v. Cinelli, 485 U.S. 1037 (1988) (White, J., dissenting from denial of cert.)
United States v. Orduno-Ramirez, 61 F.4th 1263 (10th Cir. 2023)

sides.position: The government must show the lack of prejudice once an intrusion is shown.
cases: Cutillo v. Cinelli, 485 U.S. 1037 (1988) (White, J., dissenting from denial of cert.)
United States v. Orduno-Ramirez, 61 F.4th 1263 (10th Cir. 2023)

quote: see Cutillo v. Cinelli, 485 U.S. 1037, 1037-38 (1988) (White, J., dissenting from denial of cert.) (noting circuit split on who bears the burden to prove prejudice).
cite: United States v. Orduno-Ramirez, 61 F.4th 1263 (10th Cir. 2023)
